page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized bare-metal-equivalent instance engineered for large-scale artificial intelligence and compute-intensive operations. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processors across an x86_64 architecture, providing 112 physical cores and 224 vCPUs clocked at 2.1 GHz. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. System memory is configured with 2952.0 GB of RAM (13.18 GB per vCPU). The server integrates an accelerator array consisting of 8 NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs delivering 1128 GB of aggregate VRAM, complemented by 12,864 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results confirm top-tier performance across parallel processing, memory throughput, and accelerated workloads. The instance achieved 180,093.2 on multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 134,560.46, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 433.75 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 1180.43 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks showed strong results, processing 5,633.5 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 196.63 tokens/sec during text generation on 7B parameter models.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density for high-throughput operational requirements, balancing immense compute parallelism with fast local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU capacity. A key engineering tradeoff is its single-core compute performance, which registers within the middle 50% on stress-ng tests (2143.28) due to the moderate 2.1 GHz base frequency. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external routing configurations for egress or public access.

Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g is targeted specifically at training large foundation models, high-throughput LLM inference, intensive deep learning workflows, ray tracing, high-volume database operations, and distributed scientific simulation workloads.
